title: ADR CRUD as an MCP tool

forkDecision.decision: Standalone MCP tool `manage_adr`, symmetric to `manage_roadmap`, with actions create/read/update/list. Not folded into the adr-fleet skill surface. Shape and registration modeled on packages/cli/src/mcp/tools/roadmap.ts.

stages.outcome: Located ADR store (docs/knowledge/decisions/NNNN-slug.md), DecisionIngestor frontmatter format, manage_roadmap registration pattern (3 sites), reference-docs generation seam, and the #1323 number-collision defect.
Added adr-store.ts (list/read/create/update + collision-safe allocateNextNumber), adr.ts MCP tool (manage_adr), registered in server.ts + tool-capability-declarations.ts, regenerated reference docs.
16 unit tests in adr.test.ts all pass; server/server-integration/tool-tiers/capabilities suites green after 106->107 count bump; tsc --noEmit clean; eslint clean on src.

assumptions: Fork A (standalone manage_adr tool) as pre-answered in the lane brief.

ADR store lives in the CLI package, not @harness-engineering/core: the CRUD surface is consumed only by the MCP tool (unlike the shared roadmap store), so no core export / core-barrel allowlist change is added.
create() allocates max(existing number)+1 zero-padded (not count+1) — the collision-free scheme required by #1323 and used by adr-fleet.
ADRs are stored in docs/knowledge/decisions/ (per #1323 note and the directory README), NOT docs/adr/ or docs/decisions/.
create() defaults status to 'proposed' and date to today, matching the never-auto-accept convention; explicit values override.
manage_adr declares 'write' scope and is NOT a network tool (local filesystem only).
The tool reuses DecisionIngestor's frontmatter format rather than importing its private parser (graph-package-internal, no create/allocate surface).
